# MEMORANDUM

**To:** [Supervising Partner]
**From:** [Associate]
**Date:** November 10, 2026
**Re:** Paikort Pet Foods, Inc. / Broumoux Distribution Co.: Review of Distribution Documents and Recommended Actions

**Documents reviewed:**

- Distribution Agreement dated March 1, 2025 (the "DA")
- Amendment No. 1 dated October 1, 2026 (the "Amendment")
- Quality Agreement dated March 1, 2025 (the "QA")
- Wilmington Office Lease dated January 15, 2025 (the "Lease")

---

## URGENT: Action Needed Before December 1, 2026

1. **Broumoux's consent to the Fenwyck merger has not been obtained (Issue 1).**
   - The merger is a Change of Control under DA §14.2.
   - Closing without Broumoux's prior written consent is a material breach. It cannot be cured.
   - It would let Broumoux terminate and collect an inventory buyback and a twelve-month Exit Fee.
   - Closing is expected on or about **December 1, 2026**, which is about three weeks away.
   - We need to go back to Broumoux now.

2. **Broumoux's recall-cost indemnity is now capped at $750,000 (Issue 2).**
   - This is not time-critical in the same way as Issue 1.
   - However, it should be fixed in the same instrument as the consent. Broumoux may treat the consent as leverage, so it is better to raise both together.

---

## Order of Precedence: How the Documents Interact

DA §16.4 resolves conflicts in this order:

1. any **Amendment** signed by both parties **prevails first**;
2. then the DA;
3. then the QA.

There is one exception: **the QA "controls quality, recall and handling matters."** This exception drives Issues 2 and 3 below.

---

## Issue 1: Pending Fenwyck Merger Requires Broumoux's Prior Written Consent (URGENT)

**Where:**
- DA §14.2 (Change of Control)
- DA §1.2 (definition of Change of Control)
- DA §14.3 (consequences)
- Amendment Recital C

**What the documents say:**
- DA §1.2(a) defines "Change of Control" to include a merger in which a party "survives but becomes a subsidiary of another entity."
- Amendment Recital C records that on September 15, 2026 Paikort signed an Agreement and Plan of Merger with Fenwyck Pet Holdings, LLC. Under it, Paikort will become a **wholly owned subsidiary** of Fenwyck, with closing expected on or about December 1, 2026. This falls squarely within §1.2(a).
- DA §14.2 provides that "Any Change of Control of Supplier requires the prior written consent of Distributor."
- Unlike assignment under §14.1, this consent is **not** subject to a "not unreasonably withheld" standard. Broumoux has full discretion.

**Consent has not been given:**
- The Amendment discloses the merger in a recital, but its operative provisions contain **no consent or waiver**.
- Amendment §6.1 instead ratifies all other terms, which includes §14.2.
- DA §16.3 requires any waiver to be in writing and signed by the waiving party.
- Nothing else in the folder records consent.
- We should not treat Broumoux's signature on an amendment that merely recites the merger as consent. That argument is weak, and it is not one to rely on before a closing.

**Why it matters for Paikort:** If the merger closes without consent:

- **No cure.** It is a material breach of the DA, and it is expressly excluded from the 30-day cure period in §13.1.
- **Termination right.** Broumoux may terminate on 30 days' notice at any time within 120 days after closing.
- **Inventory buyback.** Under §14.3(a), Paikort must repurchase all saleable inventory at Broumoux's purchase price plus freight, and take delivery within 30 days.
- **Exit Fee.** Under §14.3(b), Paikort must pay twelve months' average Gross Margin on Broumoux's Product sales, within 30 days.
  - Under the minimum purchase commitment (Exhibit B: $3.5M–$4M per year), this could be a seven-figure sum.
- **Uncapped.** Both §14.3 payments are carved out of the $750,000 cap and the consequential-damages exclusion by §11.3(d).
- **Leverage for Broumoux.** For four months after closing, Broumoux holds an option to exit on favorable terms or to renegotiate.
- **Deal risk.** This exposure may also need to be disclosed to Fenwyck. It may implicate Paikort's representations, consent covenants or closing conditions in the merger agreement. We should check the merger agreement's third-party consent schedule.

**Recommended fix (requires going back to Broumoux):**

1. Send Broumoux formal written notice of the proposed Change of Control under §14.2, if this has not already been done in compliance with §16.1, and request consent immediately.
2. Obtain a signed consent and waiver **before closing**. Ideally, document it in Amendment No. 2 together with the fix in Issue 2.
3. Coordinate with deal counsel on the merger agreement's consent and closing provisions, and on what Fenwyck has been told.

**Proposed language (Consent and Waiver):**

> **Consent to Change of Control.** Distributor acknowledges that it has received written notice under Section 14.2 of the Agreement of the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated September 15, 2026 between Supplier and Fenwyck Pet Holdings, LLC ("**Fenwyck**"), under which Supplier will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Fenwyck (the "**Fenwyck Transaction**"). For purposes of Section 14.2 of the Agreement, Distributor irrevocably consents to the Fenwyck Transaction and to any related Change of Control of Supplier. Distributor waives any right to treat the Fenwyck Transaction as a breach of the Agreement, to terminate the Agreement under Section 14.2, or to receive any payment or repurchase under Section 14.3 in connection with the Fenwyck Transaction. This consent extends to any post-closing internal reorganization in which Supplier remains, directly or indirectly, controlled by Fenwyck.

**Longer-term point:** Paikort should also consider proposing to limit or delete §14.2 and §14.3 going forward. For example, the consent right could apply only to a Change of Control in favor of a direct competitor of Broumoux. Broumoux may resist, and we should not let that negotiation delay the consent itself.

---

## Issue 2: Amendment No. 1 Caps Broumoux's Recall-Cost Indemnity at $750,000

**Where:**
- Amendment No. 1, §3, which restates DA §11.3(b)
- Read with DA §§10.1, 10.2, 11.1, 11.2 and QA §8.3

**What changed:**
- Originally, DA §11.3(b) excluded from the liability limits "a party's indemnification obligations under **Section 10.1 or Section 10.2**."
- Amendment §3 restates it as "a Party's indemnification obligations under **Section 10.1(a) or Section 10.2**."

**Effect:**
- **Paikort's indemnities stay uncapped.** All of §10.2 remains carved out: product injury claims, recalls not caused by Broumoux, and IP claims.
- **Broumoux keeps only one uncapped indemnity.** Only §10.1(a), for third-party bodily and animal injury claims, remains carved out.
- **Two Broumoux indemnities are now capped.** These now fall under the **$750,000 aggregate per-party cap in DA §11.2**:
  - **§10.1(c)**, Broumoux's indemnity for Recall, withdrawal and destruction costs caused by its storage or handling failures; and
  - **§10.1(b)**, its indemnity for breaching the territory and non-compete restrictions in §§2.3–2.4.
- **The consequential-damages exclusion also now applies to those claims.** §11.1 is subject to the same exclusions. Recall-related losses that could be characterized as lost profits or consequential damages are therefore also at risk.
- **The Amendment prevails.** Under DA §16.4 the Amendment ranks first, so the narrowed carve-out controls.
- **The QA does not help.** QA §8.3 allocates handling-caused recall costs to Broumoux only "as indemnifiable under Section 10.1(c) of the Distribution Agreement." That allocation therefore picks up the cap rather than overriding it.
- **The change was not flagged.** The Amendment's recitals describe it as adding the freeze-dried line and "related conforming changes." Nothing signals a shift in risk allocation.

**Why it matters for Paikort:**

- **Recall costs can exceed the cap.** A multi-state pet food recall covering NJ, NY and PA can easily run past $750,000 across notification, retrieval, destruction, replacement, regulatory response and customer credits.
  - Example: a warehouse temperature or humidity excursion in breach of QA §4.2 (80°F / 65% RH), or pest contamination.
- **The new product line raises the risk.** Freeze-dried products, just added, are moisture-sensitive (QA §5.4).
- **Recovery is limited.** Paikort's recovery for a Broumoux-caused recall is now limited to $750,000 in aggregate. That figure covers **all** of Broumoux's capped liability under the DA, not recalls alone.
- **The exposure is one-sided.** Paikort's own §10.2 exposure remains uncapped.
- **Insurance does not close the gap.** Recall insurance required under DA §12.1(b) is only $1,000,000.
- **The territory indemnity is weakened too.** The §10.1(b) cap reduces Paikort's remedy for grey-market or out-of-territory diversion.

**Recommended fix (requires going back to Broumoux):**

- Restore the original carve-out by a further amendment, ideally Amendment No. 2 alongside the consent in Issue 1.
- We should also ask the client whether this change was negotiated or slipped in. That will shape how we raise it with Broumoux.

**Proposed language:**

> **Amendment to Section 11.3(b).** Section 11.3(b) of the Agreement, as amended by Amendment No. 1, is amended to read in full:
>
> "(b) a Party's indemnification obligations under Section 10.1 (including Sections 10.1(a), 10.1(b) and 10.1(c)) or Section 10.2;"
>
> The Parties confirm that, with effect from the Amendment Effective Date of Amendment No. 1, Distributor's obligations under Section 10.1(c) of the Agreement and Section 8.3 of the Quality Agreement are not subject to the limitations in Sections 11.1 or 11.2.

**Fallback position:** If Broumoux will not restore the uncapped position, negotiate a separate, materially higher cap for §10.1(c). Two options:

- a fixed amount, for example not less than Broumoux's recall insurance limit plus a multiple; or
- a requirement that Broumoux raise its product contamination and recall insurance limits under DA §12.1(b), with Paikort named as additional insured or loss payee.

---

## Issue 3: Quality Agreement Sends Recall and Handling Disputes to New Jersey Law and Essex County Courts

**Where:**
- QA §12 (Governing Law and Venue), specifically §§12.1–12.2
- These conflict with DA §15.1 (Delaware law) and DA §15.2 (exclusive jurisdiction of state or federal courts in New Castle County, Delaware)
- Read with DA §16.4

**What the documents say:**

- **DA §15.1–15.2.** The DA and any dispute "arising out of or relating to it" are governed by the **laws of the State of Delaware**, in the courts of **New Castle County, Delaware**. Amendment §7.1 carries the same clauses into the Amendment.
- **QA §12.1.** All disputes "arising under or relating to" the QA, **expressly including disputes concerning the allocation of Recall costs and the storage and handling of Products**, are governed by the **laws of the State of New Jersey**.
- **QA §12.2.** Such actions must be brought **exclusively** in the state or federal courts located in **Essex County, New Jersey**.
- **DA §16.4.** The QA normally ranks last. However, it "controls quality, recall and handling matters." The precedence clause therefore does not resolve the conflict in favor of Delaware. It hands recall and handling disputes to the QA's New Jersey clause.

**Why it matters for Paikort:**

- **The highest-value disputes are the ones at stake.** Recall and handling disputes are the most likely and most expensive claims Paikort would bring against Broumoux.
- **Split proceedings.** A claim for recall costs under DA §10.1(c) and QA §8.3, brought in Delaware under DA §15.2, could be met with a motion to dismiss or transfer based on the QA's exclusive Essex County forum. Paikort could end up litigating:
  - recall-cost allocation in New Jersey; and
  - related claims in Delaware, such as the cap question in Issue 2, payment claims or territory breaches.
- **Different law on the same facts.** The outcome could turn on different substantive law, applied by different courts, to the same events.
- **Home-court advantage for Broumoux.** Broumoux is a New Jersey corporation, so the New Jersey forum favors it. Paikort chose Delaware for the DA for a reason.
- **Added cost and threshold litigation.** Expect forum and choice-of-law fights before reaching the merits. Note also that the DA's jury waiver (§15.4) does not appear in the QA.
- **The clause survives termination.** QA §11.2 makes §12 survive, so the problem persists after termination.

**Recommended fix (requires going back to Broumoux; both documents need bilateral signature under DA §16.3 and QA §13.2):**

- **Preferred option:** conform QA §12 to the DA.

> **Amendment to Quality Agreement Section 12.** Section 12 of the Quality Agreement is deleted and replaced in full with the following:
>
> "12. **GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTES.** This Quality Agreement and all disputes arising under or relating to it, including disputes concerning the allocation of Recall costs and the storage and handling of Products, are governed by Sections 15.1 through 15.4 of the Distribution Agreement, which apply to this Quality Agreement as if set out in full in it. Any such dispute shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in New Castle County, Delaware."

- **Belt-and-braces option:** also amend DA §16.4 so that the QA's control of operational matters cannot be read to reach dispute-resolution terms.

> **Amendment to Section 16.4.** The following is added at the end of Section 16.4 of the Agreement: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Sections 10, 11 and 15 of this Agreement control over any conflicting provision of the Quality Agreement, including any provision concerning governing law, forum or venue, and the Quality Agreement's control of quality, recall and handling matters extends only to operational requirements and does not extend to the allocation of liability, limitation of liability, governing law, forum or dispute resolution."

**Timing:** Both changes can be packaged into the same Amendment No. 2 / QA amendment round as Issues 1 and 2.

---

## Additional Observations (Lower Priority)

1. **QA review on the new product line (QA §13.3).**
   - The parties must review the QA on the addition of any new product line.
   - With the freeze-dried line added on October 1, 2026, this review is now due. Use it as the vehicle for the QA §12 fix.
   - Confirm that Paikort has furnished freeze-dried handling instructions (Amendment §5.2; QA §5.4). Broumoux's handling obligations, and therefore its recall indemnity, depend on these instructions being in place.

2. **Insurance limits (DA §12.1(b)).**
   - $1,000,000 of recall insurance is light for a three-state exclusive distribution of moisture-sensitive freeze-dried products.
   - Consider raising it in the same amendment.

3. **Drafting clean-up.**
   - The original DA §11.3(b) uses lowercase "party." The Amendment corrected this.
   - The restatement proposed in Issue 2 keeps the defined term "Party."

---

## Wilmington Office Lease: No Bearing on the Distribution Relationship

- The Lease is between Ostrel Commons Properties LLC and Paikort for Suite 610 in Wilmington, which is Paikort's sales office.
- Broumoux is not a party, and nothing in the Lease affects the distribution documents.
- For completeness: Lease §11.2(c) treats a merger in which Paikort becomes a subsidiary as a Permitted Transfer. No landlord consent is needed for the Fenwyck merger, only written notice within 30 days after closing. Deal counsel should diarize that notice.
- No further action is needed on the Lease for this matter.

---

## Summary of Recommended Actions

| # | Issue | Location | Action | Requires Broumoux? | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Change of Control consent for Fenwyck merger not obtained | DA §14.2 (with §§1.2, 14.3; Amendment Recital C) | Give §14.2 notice; obtain signed consent and waiver before ~Dec 1, 2026 closing; coordinate with deal counsel | Yes | **Urgent** |
| 2 | Recall-cost (and territory) indemnity now capped at $750,000 | Amendment No. 1 §3 (restated DA §11.3(b)) | Amendment No. 2 restoring full §10.1 carve-out; fallback: higher recall-specific cap plus insurance | Yes | High |
| 3 | QA sends recall and handling disputes to NJ law and Essex County courts | QA §12 vs. DA §§15.1–15.2, 16.4 | Conform QA §12 to Delaware law and forum; amend DA §16.4 so §15 controls | Yes | High |
| — | Office Lease | Lease | No bearing; post-closing notice under §11.2 only | No | — |

I suggest we present Issues 1–3 to Broumoux as a single package: Amendment No. 2 to the DA plus a QA amendment, signed before the Fenwyck closing. I can prepare the full draft on your sign-off.

## Issue 1: The Fenwyck Merger Is a Change of Control That Requires Broumoux's Prior Written Consent, and No Consent Has Been Obtained

**Where it appears:**
- Distribution Agreement Section 14.2 (Change of Control).
- Distribution Agreement Section 1.2 (definition of Change of Control).
- Distribution Agreement Section 14.3 (consequences of termination).
- Amendment No. 1 Recital C (disclosure of the merger).

**What the documents say:**
- **Section 1.2(a)** defines a Change of Control to include a merger in which a party "survives but becomes a subsidiary of another entity."

Under that agreement Paikort will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Fenwyck, with closing expected on or about December 1, 2026. This falls squarely within Section 1.2(a).

  - Any "Change of Control of Supplier requires the prior written consent of Distributor."

- **Section 14.3:** if Broumoux terminates on this basis, Paikort must:
  - repurchase all saleable inventory at Broumoux's purchase price plus documented freight, taking delivery within 30 days; and
  - pay an **Exit Fee** equal to twelve months' average Gross Margin on Broumoux's sales of Products.

**Consent has not been given:**
- Amendment No. 1 is the only document Broumoux signed after the merger was disclosed. It contains no consent to, or waiver of, the Change of Control.
- Recital C only records that Paikort "informed" Broumoux of the merger. That likely satisfies Paikort's separate notice obligation under Section 14.2, but notice is not consent.
- Section 6.1 of the Amendment ratifies all other terms of the Agreement "in full force and effect," which includes Section 14.2.
- Section 16.3 provides that no waiver is effective unless it is in writing and signed by the waiving party.
- Nothing else in the folder records Broumoux's consent.

**Why it matters for Paikort:**
- **No chance to cure.** The breach becomes complete at closing. Because Section 14.2 excludes the cure period, Paikort cannot fix it afterwards.
- **Uncapped Exit Fee.** Section 11.3(d) excludes Section 14.3 payment obligations from the $750,000 cap, so the Exit Fee is not limited by the cap.
  - Based on the Exhibit B minimum purchase commitment ($3.5M in contract year 2, $4M thereafter), the Exit Fee plus the inventory repurchase could be substantial.
  - Adding freeze-dried volume will increase the Gross Margin base.
- **Lost route to market.** Paikort would lose its exclusive distributor in a three-state territory.
- **Negotiating leverage for Broumoux.** Broumoux's consent right is unqualified. There is no "not unreasonably withheld" standard, unlike assignment under Section 14.1. Broumoux can therefore use it to extract price, term or other concessions.
- **Deal risk.** The merger agreement likely contains representations about material contracts and third-party consents. An unconsented Change of Control here may also create exposure to Fenwyck. This should be checked against the merger agreement's disclosure schedules and closing conditions.

**Recommended fix (requires going back to Broumoux, immediately):**
1. Request Broumoux's written consent now, in a stand-alone signed instrument delivered well before the December 1 closing.
2. Coordinate with Fenwyck's deal counsel. Confirm whether this consent is a closing condition, and whether the expected closing date can slip if consent is delayed.
3. Proposed consent and waiver language:

> **CONSENT AND WAIVER**

> Broumoux Distribution Co. ("Distributor") acknowledges receipt of notice from Paikort Pet Foods, Inc. ("Supplier") of the Agreement and Plan of Merger dated September 15, 2026 between Supplier and Fenwyck Pet Holdings, LLC ("Fenwyck"), under which Supplier will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Fenwyck (the "Transaction"). For purposes of Section 14.2 of the Distribution Agreement dated as of March 1, 2025, as amended (the "Agreement"), Distributor hereby irrevocably consents to the Transaction and to any Change of Control of Supplier resulting from it. Distributor agrees that the consummation of the Transaction (a) does not constitute a breach of the Agreement; (b) does not give rise to any right of Distributor to terminate the Agreement under Section 14.2; and (c) does not give rise to any obligation of Supplier under Section 14.3, including any obligation to repurchase inventory or pay the Exit Fee. This consent is given in accordance with Section 16.3 of the Agreement and binds Distributor and its successors and assigns.

4. **Optional, for longer-term protection:** if Broumoux is willing, amend Section 14.2 so that future intra-group restructurings and transfers to Affiliates of the Fenwyck group do not require consent.
5. **Fallback:** if Broumoux refuses or demands significant concessions, the client must decide whether to:
   - delay closing;
   - accept the termination and Exit Fee risk, quantified and allocated with Fenwyck; or

## Issue 2: The Quality Agreement Sends Recall and Handling Disputes to New Jersey Law and Essex County Courts

**Where it appears:**
- Quality Agreement Section 12 (Governing Law and Venue), Sections 12.1 and 12.2.
- This conflicts with Distribution Agreement Sections 15.1–15.2.
- The conflict is not resolved by Distribution Agreement Section 16.4.

**What the documents say:**
- **Distribution Agreement Sections 15.1–15.2:**
  - The Agreement and "any dispute arising out of or relating to it" are governed by **Delaware** law.
  - The parties submit to the **exclusive** jurisdiction of the state or federal courts in **New Castle County, Delaware**.
- **Quality Agreement Section 12.1:**
  - All disputes "arising under or relating to" the Quality Agreement are governed by the **laws of the State of New Jersey**.
  - This expressly includes "disputes concerning the allocation of Recall costs and the storage and handling of Products."
- **Quality Agreement Section 12.2:**
  - Any such action must be brought **exclusively** in the state or federal courts in **Essex County, New Jersey**.
  - This again expressly covers recall cost allocation and storage and handling disputes.
- **Distribution Agreement Section 16.4:**
  - Normally ranks the Quality Agreement last.
  - However, it gives the Quality Agreement control over "quality, recall and handling matters." The precedence clause therefore does not resolve the conflict in Delaware's favor. It arguably makes the New Jersey clause govern exactly the recall and handling disputes.
- **Survival:** Quality Agreement Section 11.2 provides that Section 12 survives termination, so the conflict outlasts the relationship.

**Why it matters for Paikort:**
- **Two-front litigation.** Recall disputes are likely to be the highest-value disputes in this relationship. A typical claim would involve several provisions:
  - a recall caused by Broumoux's warehouse failures (for example, temperature excursions above the 80°F limit in Quality Agreement Section 4.2);
  - recall-cost indemnity under Distribution Agreement Section 10.1(c); and
  - cost allocation under Quality Agreement Section 8.3.

  That claim touches both agreements. If Paikort sues in Delaware, Broumoux, a New Jersey corporation, could move to dismiss or transfer under the Quality Agreement's exclusive Essex County clause. Broumoux could also file first in New Jersey. Either way, Paikort risks parallel proceedings and threshold fights over forum.
- **Different law.** The outcome of indemnity, causation and allocation questions may differ under New Jersey law, depending on the issue.
- **Home-court advantage for Broumoux.** The New Jersey forum favors Broumoux and works against Paikort's choice of its own Delaware home forum.
- **Freeze-dried line increases the risk.** Amendment No. 1 Section 5.1 brings the new freeze-dried line under the Quality Agreement for all purposes. Freeze-dried products carry heightened pathogen and moisture sensitivity, so the recall risk and the reach of the New Jersey clause both grow.

**Recommended fix (requires going back to Broumoux; package it with the Issue 1 consent):**

Option A is preferred. Amend Quality Agreement Section 12 to conform to the Distribution Agreement:

> **12. GOVERNING LAW AND VENUE.** This Quality Agreement and all disputes arising under or relating to it, including disputes concerning the allocation of Recall costs and the storage and handling of Products, are governed by Section 15 of the Distribution Agreement, which applies to this Quality Agreement as if set out in full in it. Without limiting the foregoing, all such disputes are governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles, and shall be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in New Castle County, Delaware.

Option B should be done in addition to Option A, or alone if Broumoux resists amending the Quality Agreement directly. Add a proviso to Distribution Agreement Section 16.4:

> ...provided, however, that the Quality Agreement controls quality, recall and handling matters; and provided further that, notwithstanding the foregoing or anything in the Quality Agreement, Sections 15.1 through 15.4 of this Agreement govern all disputes arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the Quality Agreement, including disputes concerning Recalls and the allocation of Recall costs, and Section 12 of the Quality Agreement shall have no further effect.

Doing both closes the gap from either direction. Under Section 16.3 of the Distribution Agreement and Section 13.2 of the Quality Agreement, either change requires a written instrument signed by both parties.

## Issue 3 (Housekeeping): The Quality Agreement Has Not Been Updated for the Freeze-Dried Line

- Quality Agreement Section 13.3 (Review).
- Quality Agreement Section 5.4 (Freeze-Dried Products).
- Amendment No. 1 Sections 5.1–5.2.

2. Prepare a short Quality Agreement amendment that adds freeze-dried-specific storage parameters and pouch-integrity inspection steps. It can be combined with the Section 12 fix in Issue 2.

## 4. Wilmington Office Lease: Not Relevant

The Wilmington office lease has no bearing on the distribution relationship.

- It is between Paikort and Ostrel Commons Properties LLC, for Suite 610 at 1400 Market Street, Wilmington.

## Summary of Action Items

| # | Issue | Location | Action | Broumoux needed? | Timing |
